drills.title: Disaster → What Will Hurt People?
drills.description: Match each disaster to the injury pattern you should expect on arrival. Fast pattern recognition = right resource request.

items.why: Collapsed structures → entrapment, crush, and crush syndrome after release.

items.prompt: Flash flood sweeps through a campground.
items.why: Floods drown, chill, and batter with debris. Never self-deploy into moving water.

items.prompt: EF-4 tornado through a mobile-home park.
items.why: Wind-borne debris impales and batters; also check for gas leaks and downed power lines.

items.prompt: Packed stadium exit gate jammed during a stampede.
items.why: People die standing up — chest compression prevents breathing.

items.prompt: Day 4 after a hurricane; family indoors with a generator.
items.why: Generators indoors or near windows are a predictable post-storm killer.

items.prompt: Week-long heat wave; elderly living alone.
items.why: Elderly, isolated, and on diuretics/psych meds are highest risk — cool aggressively.

items.prompt: Chlorine tanker ruptures near a school.
items.why: Chemical release = respiratory toxicity. Approach upwind/uphill; decon before treatment.

items.prompt: Train derailment, two cars on their sides.
items.why: High-energy blunt trauma with extrication needs. Get the passenger manifest — it's closed.
Thermal burns, airway burns, and smoke toxins. Protect your evacuation route.

options: Biological disaster — slow surge over weeks
items.why: Biological disasters are 'slow MCIs': staff protection, PPE, and crisis standards of care matter most.
